requiredFindings.title: Native file creation happens before any ledger charge; a budget refusal leaves an uncharged file
requiredFindings.detail: create_private_regular_file opens with O_CREAT|O_EXCL before anything touches `work`; the first charge is inside prepare_fresh_private_sample. Probe C1: with a ledger limited to {1 object, 1 edge, 1 byte} the call returns Err(Capture(Budget(Edges))), the new file exists afterwards, and the ledger records (0, 0, 0). This is the charge-after-native-work defect class held throughout 447-452 and contradicts the ledger's effect contract (reserve the effect and all required follow-up work before the action).
requiredFindings.fix: Use work.effect(create_cost, capture_cost + append_cost + capture_cost, |post| { create; capture_reserved; append_reserved; capture_reserved; judge }) with a reserved-path preparation variant and a documented create cost; add a C1-shaped test proving an insufficient ledger refuses before the file exists.

observations.summary: A refusal after creation (access, capture, append) leaves an empty file, often with inherited ACEs, and retries with that name fail AlreadyExists (C2). Document the residual file or remove it handle-relatively (unlinkat on the retained parent after an inode identity check).

The parent is a kernel-resolved &Path (symlinked components followed, C6; relative paths depend on CWD). The platform already provides RetainedDirectory handle-relative creation (openat O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW). Before any caller, take an admitted RetainedDirectory so creation is bound to the admitted parent.

mode(0o600) is subject to umask; a restrictive umask yields a non-0600 file that the exact-shape gate refuses, leaving an orphan. Set the mode on the descriptor with file.set_permissions(Permissions::from_mode(0o600)) after creation.
Only a/b is tested; the empty/./.. checks are defence in depth (create_new refuses them anyway, so N2/N3 survive). Add explicit Name cases (and non-UTF-8) asserting nothing is created.
